title: Evaluating Large Language Models for automatic analysis of teacher simulations
abstract: arXiv:2407.20360v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Digital Simulations (DS) provide safe environments where users interact with an agent through conversational prompts, providing engaging learning experiences that can be used to train teacher candidates in realistic classroom scenarios. These simulations usually include open-ended questions, allowing teacher candidates to express their thoughts but complicating an automatic response analysis. To address this issue, we have evaluated Large Language Models (LLMs) to identify characteristics (user behaviors) in the responses of DS for teacher education. translated_title: 评估大型语言模型在教师模拟自动分析中的应用
translated_abstract: 数字模拟（DS）提供了安全的环境，用户可以通过对话提示与代理交互，提供引人入胜的学习体验，可用于在逼真的课堂场景中培训教师候选人。这些模拟通常包含开放式问题，允许教师候选人表达自己的想法，但使自动响应分析变得复杂。为解决此问题，我们评估了大型语言模型（LLMs）来识别教师教育数字模拟响应中的特征（用户行为）。我们评估了DeBERTaV3和Llama 3的性能，结合零样本、少样本和微调方法。实验发现，LLMs的性能因需识别的特征不同而有显著差异。类似的差异也出现在Phi-4-mini和Qwen-3中。此外，我们注意到DeBERTaV3在识别新特征时性能显著下降。
tldr: 本研究评估了多种大型语言模型（如DeBERTaV3、Llama 3等）在自动分析教师模拟中开放式响应特征的能力，发现性能因特征类型而异，且模型在处理新特征时表现不稳定。
en_tdlr: This study evaluates various large language models (e.g., DeBERTaV3, Llama 3) for automatically analyzing features in open-ended responses from teacher simulations, finding performance varies by feature type and models degrade on novel features.
